note.explanation: Natural systems exist in nature and operate without human involvement. Artificial systems are made by people for particular functions or purposes. To identify a system, ask whether it occurs naturally or has been created by people.
note.checkAnswer: A galaxy is a natural system because it occurs in nature. A screw gauge is an artificial system because people make it.
note.simple: Natural means found in nature; artificial means made by people.
note.checkQuestion: Is a galaxy a natural system or an artificial system?
note.title: Natural and artificial systems
steps: Ask whether the system exists in nature without people making it.
If it does, classify it as a natural system.
If people created it for a function or purpose, classify it as an artificial system.
note.answer: Natural systems occur in nature; artificial systems are created by people for particular functions or purposes.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is a natural system?
rationales: A forest is a natural system that exists in nature.
A screw gauge is made by people, so it is artificial.
A bridge is constructed by people, so it is artificial.
A database is created and managed using software, so it is artificial.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is an artificial system?
rationales: An ocean occurs in nature and is a natural system.
A galaxy occurs in nature and is a natural system.
A robotic arm is designed and made by people, so it is artificial.
An atom is a natural physical system.

mcqs.stem: Which example is a social system?

A university is an academic institution and a social system.
A hydrogen atom is part of a natural physical system.
A galaxy is a natural physical system.

modelAnswer: Natural systems are those that exist in nature and operate independently of human involvement.
They are governed by natural laws and processes.
Examples include atoms, cells, forests, oceans, and the cosmos.
Artificial systems are created and developed by people so that they may fulfill certain functions or address certain issues.
They are deliberately designed to perform tasks, improve efficiency, or provide solutions to issues.
Examples include a screw gauge, a bridge, a database, and a university.
Therefore, natural systems occur without people creating them, while artificial systems are made by people for particular purposes.

explain.title: Two broad types
explain.body: Systems can be broadly categorized into two types: natural and artificial. Natural systems occur in nature; artificial systems are made by people.

explain.title: Natural systems
explain.body: Natural systems are those that exist in nature and operate independently of human involvement. They are governed by natural laws and processes. Examples include atoms, cells, forests, oceans, and the cosmos.

explain.title: Kinds of natural systems
explain.body: Physical systems are composed of physical components and governed by the laws of physics. Chemical systems involve substances and their interactions, transformations, and reactions. Biological systems consist of living organisms and their interactions. Psychological systems involve the mind and behavior, including thoughts, emotions, and mental processes.

explain.title: Artificial systems
explain.body: Artificial systems are created and developed by people so that they may fulfill certain functions or address certain issues. They are designed to perform tasks, improve efficiency, or provide solutions.

explain.title: Kinds of artificial systems
explain.body: Knowledge systems help capture, process, store, retrieve, and manage information. Engineering systems apply engineering concepts to tasks and technical challenges. Social systems organize social interactions, governance, and community activities. Examples include databases, bridges, and academic institutions.

mistakes: Do not call something natural just because it is large or complicated; classify it by whether it occurs in nature or is made by people.
Do not describe an artificial system as something that occurs independently of human involvement.
Do not give an example without identifying which type it belongs to.
Do not confuse a system's type with its size: artificial systems can be small or large.
